project_specification.overview: Scholium is a decentralized preprint and peer-review network: the arXiv you can verify, review in the open, and never lose. Every paper, version, review and decision is a signed, content-addressed record appended to a hash-chained event log that any reader can verify offline. This spec builds the Phase 1 Community MVP from docs/PRD.md section 5 (signed records and export, identity with tiers 0-4, upload/sanitize/moderate/list, viewer, annotations and search, discussion and escrowed formal review, advisory AI pre-review). Phase 2-4 capabilities (IPFS/cold storage, on-chain anchoring, ZK review, DOIs, governance, reputation, federation) are out of scope; anchor status is always reported as pending. Source documents: docs/PRD.md (requirements), docs/tech_architect.md (architecture), docs/design.md (UX/UI, the authority for every screen). docs/scholium-poc.html is a journey prototype for reference only; never copy its layout over design.md.
project_specification.target_audience: Authors (PhD students publishing 2-4 papers a year), reviewers (senior researchers who want verifiable credit while staying anonymous), readers (ML engineers who need to know whether a paper was checked), volunteer moderators (category editors), and library node operators. Pilot community: AI/ML researchers.

frontend.framework: Next.js 15 App Router (each feature owns a route group apps/web/src/app/(feature)/ plus apps/web/src/features/feature/)
frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with design.md tokens as CSS variables

backend.framework: Python 3.12 FastAPI, one app with modules under apps/api/src/app/modules/* discovered by module_loader.py
backend.orm: SQLAlchemy 2.0 (sync); each module declares its own models in its own package
backend.record_core: apps/api/packages/record-core (python package scholium_record_core): DAG-CBOR, CIDv1, Ed25519, did:key, sch: ids, JSON Schemas, verifier. Replaces the Rust record-core of tech_architect.md for the MVP; the TypeScript port lives in apps/web/src/features/verify-core and both are pinned by shared test vectors
backend.testing: pytest with pytest-xdist -n 2, FastAPI TestClient, JOBS_EAGER=1

database.primary: SQLite (DATABASE_URL) with FTS5 for full-text search; tables created from module models at startup

communication.api_style: REST under /v1; every write is a client-signed record envelope; errors are RFC 9457 problem details
communication.auth: did:key challenge-response sign-in, 15-minute access tokens, rotating refresh tokens

infrastructure.ai: Pluggable LLM providers: fake (tests), Anthropic (hosted, public papers only), Ollama (self-hosted)
infrastructure.sandbox: docker run --network none for reproduction runs when docker is available

project_specification.prerequisites: - Python 3.12 with uv; Node.js 22+ with pnpm - Optional: docker for reproduction runs, clamd for antivirus, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for hosted AI review, OLLAMA_URL for self-hosted models - Environment variables documented in .env.example: DATABASE_URL, CONTENT_DIR, NODE_KEY_PATH, JWT_SECRET, COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY, ORCID_BASE_URL, ORCID_CLIENT_ID, ORCID_CLIENT_SECRET, ORCID_MOCK, ARXIV_MOCK, AI_PROVIDER, AI_HOSTED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL, SMTP_URL, JOBS_EAGER, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL - Root `npm test` runs the api pytest suite and the web vitest suite; `npm run test:e2e` runs Playwright
project_specification.constraints: - Never store personal data or paper content on a blockchain. - Do not add a tradable token or token-weighted votes. - Never let AI review output change paper status, listing or reputation; no code path from ai_review to papers.status. - Never hold a user's private signing key on the server; the server only ever sees public keys and signatures. - Process unlisted drafts only with self-hosted or fake AI providers. - Run paper reproduction only in an isolated sandbox with no network. - Pass paper text to AI agents as quoted data in a separate block, never concatenated into instructions. - Never update or delete rows in the event_log table. - Never render AI output in the colours of human review status; --ai is reserved for AI pre-review. - Never convey status by colour alone; always icon plus word. - Return API errors as RFC 9457 problem details. - Keep personal data only in the encrypted, erasable profile table. - Do not show like or vote counts on papers. - Meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, keyboard access to everything, focus rings 2px accent. - Follow docs/design.md for every screen, token, component and microcopy; docs/scholium-poc.html is reference only. - Modules register routers and record handlers from their own package; never edit main.py or module_loader.py after the foundation.

feature.description: System foundation: Scaffold the workspace skeleton (creates root package.json whose test script runs the api pytest suite then the web vitest suite, .env.example, apps/api uv project with [tool.uv.workspace] members packages/* (record-core and cli package skeletons), FastAPI app factory in apps/api/src/app/main.py with module_loader.py importing every apps/api/src/app/modules/* package and mounting its optional router under /v1 and calling its optional on_startup hook, settings.py, db.py (SQLAlchemy 2.0 sync engine, SQLite via DATABASE_URL, a declarative Base whose metadata create_all runs after modules load), GET /healthz that returns 200, pytest config with -n 2 and testpaths covering src and packages, and apps/web Next.js 15 App Router TypeScript Tailwind shell with root layout.tsx and vitest.config.ts using maxWorkers 2; it pins every dependency the spec names (fastapi, sqlalchemy, pydantic, pyjwt, cryptography, pynacl, dag-cbor, multiformats, pypdf, httpx, anthropic, pytest, pytest-xdist; next, react, tailwindcss, @ipld/dag-cbor, multiformats, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, tus-js-client, vitest, @testing-library/react, @playwright/test); every python command runs as uv run --all-packages so workspace packages are importable)

API returns every error as an RFC 9457 problem details JSON body (type, title, status, detail, instance) with content type application/problem+json, including 422 with a field-level errors array on validation failure

System issues 15-minute access tokens and exposes a require_tier(n) FastAPI dependency that returns 403 problem details naming the required tier and the caller tier when a principal's trust tier (0 Reader, 1 Member, 2 Author, 3 Reviewer, 4 Moderator) is too low
Background job runner persists queued jobs to the jobs table and runs registered job handlers on a worker thread, running them inline when JOBS_EAGER=1 so tests are synchronous

API middleware throttles writes per trust tier and per account age (new accounts get 20 posts per day) and returns 429 problem details with Retry-After plus an X-RateLimit-Remaining header on every write

System computes a record id as a CIDv1 (dag-cbor codec, sha2-256) over the DAG-CBOR encoding of the envelope fields v, type, author, created, prev, body, proofs (excluding id and sig) and writes cross-language test vectors to vectors/records.json
System signs and verifies Ed25519 signatures over the canonical envelope bytes and converts Ed25519 public keys to and from did:key identifiers, that returns False for a tampered body
System computes raw-codec CIDv1 sha2-256 file ids for file bytes and validates a manifest body of files with path, cid, size, mediaType and role fields

System derives the stable sch: short id (12 base32 characters of the genesis CID plus a checksum grouped xxxx-xxxx-xxxx) and parses sch:xxxx-xxxx-xxxx/vN version ids, and returns a ValueError error message on a bad checksum

System validates record bodies against JSON Schemas shipped in schemas/ for every Phase 1 record type (paper.genesis, paper.version, manifest, coauthor.consent, review.commit, review.formal, review.response, review.rating, discussion.post, ai.review, rendition, endorsement, moderation.decision, appeal, appeal.decision, retraction, correction, withdrawal, key.rotation, erasure.request, external.mirror, flag) and returns a list of error messages

System verifies a paper from a set of records by following prev links from newest version to genesis, checking each signature, each prev hash, a consent from every listed author and applying retraction, correction and tombstone supersession, that returns a report with status, signers, version_count and per-check results

System persists each accepted record to the event_log table with seq, record_cid, record_type, author_did, body, raw canonical bytes, prev_hash, entry_hash = sha256(prev_hash || record_cid || raw) and origin_node, and notifies in-process subscribers registered with ledger.subscribe(record_type, fn)
Database triggers on the event_log table reject UPDATE and DELETE statements so the log is append-only, raising an integrity error message
API exposes GET /v1/sync/head that returns the node-signed log head (node_did, seq, entry_hash, signature) using the node Ed25519 key loaded from NODE_KEY_PATH
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/sync/head returns 200 with seq, entry_hash, node_did and signature fields - The signature in the GET /v1/sync/head response verifies against the node_did public key

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/records/{cid} that returns the stored signed envelope as JSON, and 404 problem details for an unknown cid
API exposes GET /v1/records/{cid}/proof that returns the record's log seq, entry_hash, prev_hash, the signed log head and anchor status pending
API exposes GET /v1/sync/range?from=&to= that returns log entries in seq order with their hashes so a third party can replay the log
System verify_log function recomputes the hash chain over a sequence of log entries and returns the first broken seq when any entry was rewritten, reordered or removed
System provides a record-type handler registry where modules call register(record_type, handler, min_tier) at import time, and lookup of an unregistered type returns 422 problem details

API exposes POST /v1/records that validates the envelope schema, recomputes the CID, verifies the signature against the author's active key, runs the type handler, appends to the ledger and returns 201 with id, shortId, state and anchor pending
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/records with an id that does not match the recomputed CID returns 422 problem details - POST /v1/records with a signature made by a different key returns 401 problem details - POST /v1/records with an unknown record type returns 422 problem details

feature.description: API rejects a POST /v1/records submission whose author tier is below the handler's min_tier with 403 problem details stating the required tier
API replays the stored 201 response when POST /v1/records repeats an Idempotency-Key, persisting keys to the idempotency_keys table
API exposes POST /v1/auth/challenge that returns a single-use nonce (expires in 5 minutes) for a did:key, saved to the auth_challenges table

API exposes POST /v1/auth/verify that checks the Ed25519 signature over the nonce, creates the account in the accounts table on first sign-in at tier 0 and returns 200 with access_token and refresh_token
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/auth/verify with a correctly signed nonce returns 200 with access_token and refresh_token - POST /v1/auth/verify with a reused nonce returns 401 problem details - POST /v1/auth/verify with a signature from another key returns 401 problem details

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/auth/refresh that rotates the refresh token, storing hashes in the refresh_tokens table, and returns 401 when a rotated-out token is reused
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/auth/refresh with a valid refresh_token returns 200 with a new refresh_token - POST /v1/auth/refresh with an already-used refresh_token returns 401

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/did/{did} that returns the DID document with the active key, the key history from key.rotation records and the account tier
System resolves the active signing key for a DID from the account_keys table so ingest rejects records signed by a key rotated out before the record arrived
API exposes POST /v1/auth/logout that revokes the caller refresh token in the refresh_tokens table and returns 204
User can save name, affiliation and email via PUT /v1/profiles/{did} (returns 200), which the system encrypts with a per-object key into profile.enc_blob with the key held in the profile_keys table
API exposes GET /v1/profiles/{did} that returns decrypted name, affiliation, ORCID iD, tier and public signed reviews, showing only the pseudonymous DID after erasure
User can erase their profile via DELETE /v1/profiles/{did}, which deletes the per-object key (crypto-shredding), appends an erasure.request record and returns 202 while their records still verify
feature.acceptance: - DELETE /v1/profiles/{did} by the owner returns 202 - After erasure GET /v1/profiles/{did} returns the DID with null name, affiliation and email - After erasure GET /v1/records/{cid} for a record the user signed still returns the signed envelope

feature.description: System sends an email verification link on PUT /v1/profiles/{did} and POST /v1/profiles/{did}/verify-email returns 200 setting email_verified, which tier 1 requires
API exposes GET /v1/auth/orcid/start that returns the ORCID authorize URL with a signed state parameter, using ORCID_BASE_URL (sandbox by default)

API exposes GET /v1/auth/orcid/callback that exchanges the code (ORCID_MOCK=1 accepts mock-<orcid> codes for tests), issues a node-signed ORCID ownership verifiable credential bound to the DID and saves it to the credentials table
feature.acceptance: - With ORCID_MOCK=1, GET /v1/auth/orcid/callback?code=mock-0000-0002-1825-0097 with a valid state returns 200 with the credential - GET /v1/profiles/{did} after linking shows the linked ORCID iD

feature.description: System stores a nullifier H(issuer || orcid || domain) in the nullifiers table so one ORCID maps to one active DID, that returns 409 problem details on a second link
System saves tier 1 Member to the accounts table once an email and an ORCID credential exist for an account at tier 0
API exposes POST /v1/credentials/present that verifies a credential presentation signature and status, that returns 200 with verified true or 422 with the failing check
User can set 5 recovery guardian DIDs via PUT /v1/me/guardians, saved to the guardians table, and submissions return 403 problem details until guardians are set
System accepts a key.rotation record signed by the old key, records the new key as active in account_keys and rejects later records signed by the old key with 401

User can open a recovery request via POST /v1/recovery/requests identified by ORCID with a new public key, which notifies each guardian and returns 201 with request_id (persisted to the recovery_requests table)
API exposes POST /v1/recovery/requests/{id}/approvals for guardian signatures and returns the approval count, opening a 72-hour contest window at 3 of 5 approvals

Background job finalizes a recovery after the 72-hour contest window by appending a key.rotation record with the guardian proofs, while POST /v1/recovery/requests/{id}/cancel signed by the old key returns 200 and cancels it
feature.acceptance: - After 3 approvals and the contest window elapsing, records signed by the old key return 401 from POST /v1/records - POST /v1/recovery/requests/{id}/cancel signed by the old key returns 200 and the old key stays active

feature.description: System accepts an endorsement record (endorsee, category, expiry) only from a tier-3 endorser, saves it to the endorsements table and grants the endorsee tier 2 Author
System exposes can_submit(did, category) that returns False for a category the author is not endorsed in, and GET /v1/me/endorsements lists active endorsements with expiry
System stores file bytes in a CID-addressed blob directory (CONTENT_DIR) and records cid, size, media_type and scan_status in the blobs table

API exposes GET /v1/content/{cid} that serves bytes only when scan_status is passed, with Content-Security-Policy sandbox, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and no cookies, that returns 423 while scanning and 451 for a tombstoned cid
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/content/{cid} for a blob still scanning returns 423 - GET /v1/content/{cid} for a passed blob returns 200 with a Content-Security-Policy header containing sandbox

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/uploads (tus 1.0 creation) that returns 201 with a Location header, rejecting a PDF over 50 MB or a bundle over 5 GB with 413 problem details
API exposes PATCH /v1/uploads/{id} appending bytes at Upload-Offset and HEAD /v1/uploads/{id} returning the current Upload-Offset, with 409 on an offset mismatch so interrupted uploads resume
feature.acceptance: - HEAD /v1/uploads/{id} after a partial PATCH returns the received Upload-Offset - PATCH /v1/uploads/{id} with a wrong Upload-Offset returns 409

feature.description: System moves a completed upload into the content store and returns its raw CID in the final PATCH response Upload-Cid header
System accepts a manifest record only when every listed file cid exists in the blobs table with a matching size, otherwise 422 problem details naming the file path
System accepts a paper.genesis record from a tier-2 author endorsed in every category, which saves to the papers table its categories, licence (default CC BY 4.0) and assigned sch: short_id

System saves to paper_versions each accepted paper.version record whose prev equals the current latest version and n is prev n + 1, keeping title, abstract, manifest, licence and change_note, plus authors with credit roles in the authorship table, in state awaiting_consent
System limits tier-2 accounts younger than 90 days to one paper.genesis per week, that returns 429 problem details with the next allowed date
System emits a version.state_changed event as paper_versions.state advances through awaiting_consent, scanning, moderation, listed, held and rejected
System accepts withdrawal, correction and retraction records from a paper author or a tier-4 member, saving them to the notices table so every version shows the notice
System accepts a coauthor.consent record (version, role, decision accept or decline) only from a DID listed on that version, saving consent_cid to the authorship table and rejecting others with 403
System keeps a version in awaiting_consent until every listed author has accepted, then moves it to scanning, while one decline returns the version to draft with the decliner named
feature.acceptance: - A version with 3 authors and 2 consents has state awaiting_consent in GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/consents - After the third consent the version state becomes scanning

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/consents that returns each author with status waiting, signed or declined
System notify(did, kind, payload) persists a row to the notifications table, emailing through SMTP when SMTP_URL is set and logging the email to the outbox otherwise
API exposes GET /v1/me/notifications that returns unread and read notifications, and POST /v1/me/notifications/{id}/read marks one read
System sends each listed co-author a consent link notification when a version enters awaiting_consent
System saves a failed result to the scan_reports table for each PDF (checked with pypdf) when it contains JavaScript, embedded files, Launch or OpenAction actions
System saves a hidden_text finding to scan_reports for hidden text in a PDF (white or near-invisible text, text under 2pt, instruction-like strings such as ignore previous instructions)

System saves bundle findings to scan_reports for path traversal, symlinks and absolute paths in zip and tar bundles, using ClamAV through clamd when CLAMD_SOCKET is set and recording av unavailable otherwise
Background job scans every file of a version in scanning state, saves scan_status to the blobs table, moves a clean version to moderation and holds a failed one with the exact failing check
System creates a node-signed rendition record listing sanitized files and tool versions after a version passes scanning
System saves extracted PDF text to the version_texts table split into paragraphs with stable paragraph ids (sha256 of normalized paragraph text)
System saves similarity_pct to the check_results table, computed against every listed paper using word 5-gram shingle Jaccard
System extracts references from version text and saves references_total and references_unresolved to check_results, resolving DOIs through Crossref only when CROSSREF_ENABLED=1
System saves metadata_match to check_results, true when the signed title appears in the first page text
API exposes GET /v1/moderation/policies that returns the policy clause list (id, title, text) loaded from policies.yaml
API exposes GET /v1/moderation/queue for tier 4 that returns versions in moderation with category, age_hours, similarity_pct, references_unresolved, scan result and new_account flag
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/moderation/queue as a tier-1 user returns 403 problem details - GET /v1/moderation/queue as a tier-4 user returns 200 with similarity_pct and scan fields per entry

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/moderation/decisions accepting a signed moderation.decision (list, hold, reclassify, reject, delist) that requires a known policy clause and a reason, saves it to the moderation_decisions table and sets the version state
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/moderation/decisions without a clause returns 422 problem details - POST /v1/moderation/decisions with action list returns 201 and the paper becomes resolvable by its sch: id - GET /v1/records/{cid} returns the decision record publicly

feature.description: System sends the submitting author a notification for each moderation decision with the action, clause and reason text
System saves a tombstoned cid to the denylist table and deletes the blob bytes, while the envelope and log entry remain and verification still passes
User can appeal a moderation decision once via POST /v1/appeals with grounds, which saves an appeal record and returns 409 on a second appeal
System saves to appeal_panels a 3-member panel of tier-3 or tier-4 members excluding the deciding moderator and the authors, seeded deterministically from the appeal cid
API exposes POST /v1/appeals/{cid}/votes for panel members; once 2 of 3 agree the system creates a node-signed appeal.decision with outcome and reasons
feature.acceptance: - Two matching panel votes on POST /v1/appeals/{cid}/votes produce an appeal.decision record retrievable from GET /v1/records/{cid} - A vote from a non-panel member returns 403

feature.description: User can flag a paper, post or review via POST /v1/flags with a reason category, which saves to the flags table and adds the flag to the moderation queue
API exposes GET /v1/flags/{id} that returns the flag status and linked decision cid, and notifies the reporter when decided
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id} accepting a sch: id, a sch: version id or a version cid and that returns title, abstract, authors, categories, licence, status, notices and version n
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/papers/sch:xxxx-xxxx-xxxx for a listed paper returns 200 with the latest version - GET /v1/papers/sch:xxxx-xxxx-xxxx/v1 returns version 1 after version 2 is listed - GET /v1/papers/{id} for an unlisted draft returns 404 to anonymous readers

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/versions that returns the version timeline with n, cid, change_note, listed_at and anchor status
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/manifest that returns files with path, cid, size, role, licence and scan status
API exposes GET /v1/papers that returns listed papers with tab latest or reviewed, category filter, sort newest, recently_reviewed or recently_updated and cursor pagination, without any vote counts
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/papers?tab=reviewed returns only papers with status reviewed - GET /v1/papers?category=cs.AI returns only cs.AI papers

feature.description: System compute_status(records) deterministically returns preprint, under_review, reviewed, contested, corrected or retracted from moderation, review and notice records only (never ai.review), with documented precedence
System saves a recomputed status to papers.status through a ledger subscription whenever a review, notice or moderation record for that paper is appended
feature.acceptance: - A listed paper with two revealed formal reviews recommending minor revisions shows status reviewed in GET /v1/papers/{id} - A paper with a retraction record shows status retracted in GET /v1/papers/{id}

feature.description: System saves into the SQLite FTS5 table search_fts each listed version's title, abstract and text through a ledger subscription
API exposes GET /v1/search?q= that returns ranked results with facet counts and filters for category, date range, status and has_code
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/search?q=<word from a listed title> returns that paper in the first 5 results - GET /v1/search?q=x&status=reviewed returns only reviewed papers with facets in the body

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/search/semantic?q= that returns listed versions ranked by cosine similarity of embeddings stored in the embeddings table from a pluggable embedder (deterministic hashing embedder by default, Ollama when OLLAMA_URL is set)
API exposes GET /v1/feeds/{category} that returns an Atom feed of newly listed papers with the sch: id and status per entry
API returns a JSON Feed 1.1 document from GET /v1/feeds/{category}?format=json
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/cite?format=bibtex|ris that returns a citation with the sch: version id and a retraction note when retracted
API exposes GET /v1/export/paper/{id}.car that returns a CARv1 archive of every record, file and log entry for the paper
API exposes GET /v1/export/user/{did}.car that returns a CARv1 archive of every record authored by the DID
API exposes GET /v1/export/archive.car that returns the complete public archive with the signed log head and excluding tombstoned bytes
API exposes GET /v1/oai?verb=ListRecords that returns OAI-PMH Dublin Core XML for listed papers
System provides `scholium verify <file.car>` that verifies the paper offline and prints the plain-language checklist, exiting 0 when verified and 1 on any signature or hash mismatch
System provides `scholium verify sch:xxxx-xxxx-xxxx/vN --node URL` that fetches records and proofs from a node and prints the same checklist and exit code
System provides `scholium verify-file <path> <sch-id>` that prints whether the file's CID matches the signed manifest, exiting 1 on mismatch
System provides `scholium rebuild <archive.car> --db <path>` that verifies the log chain and every record, rebuilds paper, version and status views into a fresh database and prints the paper count
System accepts discussion.post records from tier-1 members, and GET /v1/papers/{id}/threads returns threads with replies ordered by helpful votes then time (persisted to the discussion_posts table)
API exposes POST /v1/papers/{id}/threads accepting a signed discussion.post and that returns 201 with the post cid
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/papers/{id}/threads by a tier-0 account returns 403 - POST /v1/papers/{id}/threads by a tier-1 member returns 201 and the post appears in GET /v1/papers/{id}/threads

feature.description: User can mark a post helpful once via POST /v1/posts/{cid}/helpful (returns 201, a repeat returns 409), which only reorders the thread and never changes papers.status
User can mute another DID via POST /v1/me/mutes (returns 201) so GET /v1/papers/{id}/threads omits their posts for that user
API exposes POST /v1/annotations accepting a signed discussion.post whose anchor names a version cid, paragraph_id, quote and offset, that returns 201
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/annotations that returns annotations grouped by paragraph_id so they re-attach to the same paragraph on reload
feature.acceptance: - An annotation created with paragraph_id P is returned under P by GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/annotations

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/papers/{id}/review-invitations that saves to review_invitations an invitation from an author or tier-4 member to a tier-3 reviewer in the paper category
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/coi-check that returns checks for not an author, no co-authorship in 3 years and different institution for the calling reviewer

API exposes POST /v1/reviews/commit accepting a review.commit (target version, commitment hash, per-paper review key, nullifier) from a tier-3 member, that returns 409 for a second review by the same person and 403 for a co-author
feature.acceptance: - A second POST /v1/reviews/commit by the same reviewer on the same paper returns 409 - POST /v1/reviews/commit by a listed co-author returns 403 - POST /v1/reviews/commit by a tier-3 non-author returns 201

feature.description: System saves each review's reviewer identity to the review_escrows table only as a sealed box Enc(committee_public_key, reviewer_did), with uniqueness tracked by an HMAC token, never the plaintext mapping

API exposes POST /v1/reviews/reveal accepting a review.formal whose commitment matches, requiring scores 1-5 with justification for soundness, evidence, reproducibility, novelty, clarity and limitations plus confidence and recommendation, and returns 422 for free-text-only
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/reviews/reveal with a report but no rubric scores returns 422 - POST /v1/reviews/reveal whose content does not match the commitment returns 422 - POST /v1/reviews/reveal with all six scores returns 201

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/reviews that returns 200 with report bodies hidden until two reviews are committed on the version or 21 days pass since the first commit, labelling anonymous reviewers Reviewer A, Reviewer B per paper
feature.acceptance: - With one committed review, GET /v1/papers/{id}/reviews as the second reviewer returns the review without its report - After a second commit, GET /v1/papers/{id}/reviews returns both reports

feature.description: User can sign a formal review with their name (signed true) so GET /v1/profiles/{did}/reviews returns it for public credit
System accepts an updated review.formal with prev pointing at the reviewer's earlier review against a newer version, so GET /v1/papers/{id}/reviews returns both in its history
API exposes POST /v1/reviews/{cid}/rating for tier-3 members who are neither the reviewer nor an author that saves a review.rating 1-5 to review_ratings
API exposes POST /v1/reviews/{cid}/response accepting a review.response from a paper author with point-by-point replies keyed by rubric dimension and saves it to review_responses
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/reviews/{cid}/response by a non-author returns 403 - POST /v1/reviews/{cid}/response by an author returns 201 and the reply appears with the review in GET /v1/papers/{id}/reviews

feature.description: System defines an LLM provider interface with a deterministic fake provider, an Anthropic provider (AI_HOSTED_MODEL default claude-sonnet-5-5) and an Ollama provider, that returns a PrivateDraftError error message when a hosted provider is asked to process an unlisted draft
System creates agent input from the sanitized version text as quoted paragraphs with ids passed in a separate data block, never concatenated into instructions, plus the hidden_text findings

Agent prompts for methodology, literature, reproducibility and integrity live in prompts/*.md and each agent returns findings with claim, severity, confidence and evidence (span, reference_id or log_line), with the prompt-set sha256 exposed as prompt_set_hash
System rejects every finding whose evidence span is not found verbatim in the paper text, whose reference_id is unknown or whose log_line is absent from the run log

Agent for reproducibility runs the code bundle with docker --network none, read-only root, CPU, memory and 10-minute time limits, that returns log lines as evidence or a not_run finding when docker is unavailable
Agent meta-reviewer creates the final findings list by merging duplicates, flagging agent disagreements and phrasing integrity findings as needs a human check, never fraud or plagiarism detected

Background job runs the agent pipeline after a version is listed and appends a node-signed ai.review record with agents, models with versions, prompt_set_hash and findings, with no code path writing papers.status (persisted to the ai_reviews table)
API exposes GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews that returns reports labelled advisory with findings grouped by agent
feature.acceptance: - With the fake provider, GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews for a listed paper returns 200 with advisory true and four agents - Every finding in GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews has an evidence object - The paper status in GET /v1/papers/{id} is unchanged after the AI review is appended

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/ai-reviews/{cid}/rebuttal for paper authors per finding_id and POST /v1/ai-reviews/{cid}/assessments for tier-3 reviewers marking a finding confirmed or wrong (both return 201), both shown in GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews
feature.acceptance: - POST /v1/ai-reviews/{cid}/rebuttal by a non-author returns 403 - A rebuttal posted by an author appears beside its finding in GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews

feature.description: API exposes POST /v1/imports/arxiv for tier 4 that creates a node-signed external.mirror record from arXiv metadata (ARXIV_MOCK=1 for tests) marked unclaimed
User can claim an imported paper by signing a paper.version that references the external.mirror cid, which saves claimed true to the papers table when the signer's ORCID matches

API exposes GET /v1/me/dashboard that returns needs_attention (consents to sign, review invitations, author replies, moderation outcomes), my_papers with status and review counts and my_reviews with sealed or revealed state
feature.acceptance: - GET /v1/me/dashboard for a co-author with a pending consent lists it in needs_attention

feature.description: API exposes GET /v1/network that returns node did, log head seq, last anchor status pending, replica summary 1 of 1 local and moderation decision counts by clause

Admin can load demo data with `uv run python -m app.modules.admin seed-demo`, which creates demo authors, reviewers and a moderator, signs records client-side with keys written to .demo-keys.json and prints the created sch: ids

project_specification.ui_layout: - Information architecture from design.md section 4: / (feed), /c/[category], /search, /p/[id][/v[n]], /submit, /review/[id], /me, /me/security, /u/[did], /mod, /network, /verify, /signin, /onboarding, /recover, /consent/[version] - Paper page: reading column max 720px plus 360px margin panel (Reviews, AI, Discussion, Versions, Files, Proof); drawer at 1024-1279px; bottom sheet under 1024px - Global nav on desktop; bottom bar (Home, Search, Submit, Inbox, Me) under 640px
project_specification.design_system: - Colour tokens, typography (Source Serif 4 reading text 18/30, Inter UI 15/22, JetBrains Mono IDs 13/18), 4px grid, radius 6/10, motion 150-200ms ease-out: exactly as docs/design.md section 3 - Components per design.md section 7; microcopy per section 8; vocabulary avoids blockchain, token, hash, CID, node in primary UI

Reviewer invited, conflict check, rubric form, commit sealed review, reveal after second commit, author responds, v2, reviewer updates, paper becomes Reviewed
Reader opens paper, Proof tab verifies in browser, result equals scholium verify CLI, downloads code bundle
Reader flags, moderator decides with clause, author appeals, panel of 3 decides, correction notice on every version
Lost device, identify by ORCID, 3 of 5 guardians approve, 72-hour window, new key active, old key rejected
